note: The shape of the Venus dive and rise (src/stops/venus/path.ts). Each is one move between two motions that run on: the hold and the close view for the dive, the close view and the travel for the rise. Shares are of the segment, 0 at its first frame time and 1 at its end. rate: the fall or climb of the logarithm of height rises over rate[0] of the segment, stays constant, and settles over the last rate[1]. turn: the window over which the camera turns from one motion's orientation to the other's. keep: the window over which the anchor moves across the frame from where one motion sees it to where the other sees it. lens: the window of the field of view. anchor: the point of the body the move is tied to, in degrees of arc ahead of the point under the twin of place.json along its heading.
handoverNote: The handover (cut/HANDOVER.md, E1 and E2), on the engine's one move (plan E). at: the share of the segment where T lies; the path of the one move does not read it. The dive hands over in frame 1343 and the rise in frame 1539, at the heights the close scene was built for (0.0210 and 0.0182 radii). pace: the flanks of the bell of the pace as shares of the segment, rise at the far end and fall at the surface view, corner the share of a flank that is rounded. The dive names its own far flank: with the film's flanks the speed of the picture at the place stepped 0.081 of the move's mean at 1268 (npm run smooth), with 0.45 no number of the dive is over. The dive also steps aside (path.sidestep, radii to the right and up in the picture of the far end, grown in over the whole dive): on the straight line of the one move the camera came in low from the side, and the nearest ground in the lower left corner of the picture lay outside the plates that hold enough detail for it (G13 red on 1303, 1306, 1307 and 1313 to 1316, up to 5.2 percent of the picture). With the step the camera comes down nearer over the place and those frames read 0.7 percent at most. The rise names the film's flanks as they stand today. turn and liftPower are values of a later commit of the engine (agent/engine-handover 2658ca7) that today's engine does not read: they are named so that the pose of both moves stays as it is when that commit lands (turn equal to pace and liftPower 0 is today's pose, as its engineer states).
settleNote: The surface view comes down before the rise lifts off (mail 472, item 2): over the last `frames` film frames of the terrain segment (1455 to 1529) the camera's drift slows along a smooth step from its own pace to the share `to` of it. Frames before 1455 keep their bytes (1440 among them). Measured with the path judge on the one move: with to 0.3 the rise has no line 'falls before its largest value' (0.238 without the ease); 0.35 reads 0.033 and 0.4 reads 0.044 against the limit 0.03.
